Empirical Research Plan  

====================================================  

1. Identification Strategy  
--------------------------------  
• Primary design: Staggered-adoption Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study decomposition.  

Why appropriate  
– The “treatment” (electronic toll collection, ETC) is introduced at different calendar years across otherwise similar toll facilities, giving natural variation in timing.  
– Pre-adoption histories are long (≈50 yrs), so parallel-trend diagnostics are feasible.  
– Toll rates change infrequently, so discrete yearly outcomes suit DID.  
– The design directly answers: “How does the toll-setting authority change rates once payment becomes less visible?”  

Augmentations  
– Sun & Abraham (2021) interaction-weighted estimators to cure heterogeneous-treatment-timing bias.  
– Two-stage least squares (2SLS) robustness: instrument facility-year electronic-payment share with event-time dummies (years-since-ETC) to map the dose-response of visibility rather than a binary adoption.  

2. Treatment and Control  
--------------------------------  
Treatment variable  
 TREATED_it = 1 if facility i has operational ETC in year t (year t ≥ ADOPT_i); 0 otherwise.  

Control group / counterfactual  
 Facilities that have not yet adopted by year t (“not-yet-treated”) provide the contemporaneous control. A small set of never-adopters serve as an additional placebo check.  

Treatment timing  
 Event date = first year transponders accepted on the facility.  

Dose variable (optional)  
 ELECSHARE_it = share of toll revenue collected electronically.  

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
--------------------------------  
A1. Parallel pre-trends: In the absence of ETC, treated and control facilities would have evolved along the same toll-rate path.  
 Plausibility: Authorities face similar political cycles and indexation rules; we can test using pre-adoption event-time coefficients.  

A2. No differential anticipation: Authorities do not raise tolls in the years just before ETC because of its forthcoming arrival.  
 Plausibility: Adoption dates often set by engineering and procurement timetables outside the control of toll-rate committees. Still testable with leads.  

A3. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): ETC adoption at facility i does not directly affect toll rates at facility j (except through common year shocks captured by year FE).  
 Plausibility: Physical substitutability across distant bridges/roads is limited; include authority-by-year FE to further absorb any within-authority spillovers.  

A4. No time-varying confounders correlated with adoption: e.g., major capital reconstruction causing simultaneous ETC and toll hike.  
 Mitigation: Control for traffic counts, capital-outlay dummies, and facility-specific linear trends.  

4. Threats to Identification & Remedies  
--------------------------------  
1. Endogenous adoption timing (early adopters more growth-constrained).  
 • Remedy:  
   – Authority-specific linear or cubic pre-trends.  
   – Include lagged traffic growth and debt-service ratios.  
   – IV robustness: use the statewide rollout year × facility fixed differences (e.g., “first transponder availability in state”) as an instrument.  

2. Conflation with capital upgrades (ETC installed during widening projects that themselves require higher tolls).  
 • Remedy: indicator for major construction years; drop facility-years with >20 % traffic disruptions; check results restricting to facilities with “retro-fit” ETC (no reconstruction).  

3. Policy anticipation by motorists/politicians around elections.  
 • Remedy: interact treatment with state-election-year dummy; allow election-year FE; show robustness to dropping election years.  

5. R Code Outline  
--------------------------------  
```r
# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # high-dim. FE and SA2020 estimators
library(did)         # Callaway & Sant’Anna
library(ggplot2)

# ---- 1. Load & Prepare Data ----
dt <- fread("toll_panel.csv")

# Key variables assumed in file:
# facility_id, authority_id, state, year, toll_nominal, adopt_year,
# elec_share, traffic, construction_dummy, election_year

# Simple constructs
dt[, treated := ifelse(!is.na(adopt_year) & year >= adopt_year, 1L, 0L)]
dt[, event_time := year - adopt_year]            # negative = pre, 0 = adoption
dt[, ln_toll := log(toll_nominal)]

# ---- 2. Main DID (Sun & Abraham) ----
# 2a. Interaction-weighted estimator
sa <- feols(ln_toll ~ sunab(adopt_year, year) |
              facility_id + year,
            data = dt, cluster = ~authority_id)

etable(sa, drop = "Sun & Abraham")

# ---- 3. Event-study plot ----
es <- aggregate(coef = coef(sa), term = names(coef(sa)), FUN = identity)
es <- es[grepl("c::", es$term),]      # keep the lead/lag terms
es[, event := as.numeric(sub(".*c::(-?\\d+).*", "\\1", term))]
ggplot(es, aes(event, coef)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype="dashed") +
  labs(x="Years since ETC adoption", y="Log toll change vs control")

# ---- 4. Robustness: add facility-specific trends ----
sa_trend <- feols(ln_toll ~ sunab(adopt_year, year) + i(year, facility_id, ref = 0) |
                    facility_id + year,
                  data = dt, cluster = ~authority_id)

# ---- 5. IV robustness using electronic-share dose ----
dt[, yrs_since := fifelse(treated==1, year - adopt_year, 0L)]
iv <- feols(ln_toll ~ elec_share |                    # 2SLS: outcome
              facility_id + year |                    # first-stage FEs
              . ~ i(yrs_since, ref = -1),             # instruments
            data = dt, cluster = ~authority_id)

# ---- 6. Save results ----
saveRDS(list(sa=sa, sa_trend=sa_trend, iv=iv), "results.rds")
```

6. Expected Results  
--------------------------------  
Theory: Lower salience lowers perceived price, reducing opposition to increases. Toll authorities face softer political constraints, so equilibrium nominal tolls should rise after ETC.  

Magnitude: I expect an average causal effect of roughly +0.20 log points (≈22 %) within ten years of adoption, with a ramp-up: 0–2 years ≈ 0–5 %, 3–6 years ≈ 10 %, 7–10 years ≈ 20 – 25 %.  

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
--------------------------------  
C1: Parallel pre-trends evidenced (placebo leads) ..................... 0.8  
C2: No anticipation (flat −4 to −1 leads) ............................ 0.7  
C3: No time-varying confounders (controls & FE) ...................... 0.6  
C4: SUTVA / limited spillovers ....................................... 0.8  
C5: Correct standard errors & heterogeneous timing correction ........ 1.0  

Total (0–5 scale) = 3.9  

I judge the design reasonably credible, with parallel-trend and endogenous-timing concerns the main remaining caveats.
